subject: Procurement & pricing alignment — hosted vs dedicated vs private
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Evans <tom.evans@acme.com>
Cc: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & procurement paths (hosted / dedicated / private)

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so your procurement and finance teams have what they need: 

- Recap: Acme wants a low-risk POC for chat-based product support, then a production rollout. Key constraints you mentioned: preferred PO-based billing for production, SOC 2 + data isolation review, and interest in marketplace procurement if it simplifies approvals (specifically AWS Marketplace).

- Commercial paths we recommend (high-level):
  1) Hosted (Redwood API, on-demand/card billing) — fastest to start, ideal for short POC. No long-term commitment; good for feature validation.
  2) Dedicated (reserved capacity / committed monthly or annual) — predictable throughput and cost; can be procured via PO and we offer discounted pricing at commit levels (we typically model 6–12 month commits).
  3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — enterprise license + support; best for strict data residency or regulatory needs. Usually an enterprise procurement + SOW.

Attachments: Redwood-Pricing-Options.pdf (pricing tiers & billing flows). I also attached a sample SOW template and a PO template that some customers use.

Questions / next steps:
- Who on your side will own PO/legal conversations? (If you want, send their contact and I’ll loop in our contracts team.)
- Do you want a short POC on hosted (card) first, with a plan to switch to Dedicated via AWS Marketplace or PO for production?
- Is SOC 2 Type II evidence sufficient, or do you need additional artifacts?

If it helps I can draft a mutual action plan and SOW for a hosted POC -> Dedicated transition. Happy to sync with your procurement/IT.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142
[Attachment: Redwood-Pricing-Options.pdf (pdf)]
From: Tom Evans <tom.evans@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & procurement paths (hosted / dedicated / private)

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifying Qs from procurement/finance side: 

1) Our procurement prefers PO for any production spend > $25k/year. For a POC under $5k we can typically do a company card, but we need a clear transition path so finance knows when to switch.
2) For dedicated capacity, what are the minimum commit terms and lead time to spin up?
3) Marketplace: AWS Marketplace would make approvals much easier for us — do you support Marketplace billing for Dedicated capacity or is it only for hosted API?

SOC 2 Type II is fine — we’ll request it from your security folks. Also please send any sample SOW language we can pre-share with our legal team.

Tom
Director, IT Procurement | Acme Retail
tom.evans@acme.com | +1 212-555-0188
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Evans <tom.evans@acme.com>
Cc: Jane Liu <jane.liu@acme.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & procurement paths (hosted / dedicated / private)

Tom — thanks, answering inline and adding Aditya (technical lead) to confirm timelines: 

> 1) Our procurement prefers PO for any production spend > $25k/year. For a POC under $5k we can typically do a company card, but we need a clear transition path so finance knows when to switch.

Understood. Our recommended flow for customers in that situation is: start POC on hosted (card) to validate functionality. If the anticipated annualized spend will exceed your PO threshold, we draft a short MOP (mutual action plan) that defines the milestone where you convert to Dedicated/PO billing (e.g., production go-live). That makes the transition explicit for finance.

> 2) For dedicated capacity, what are the minimum commit terms and lead time to spin up?

Typical commit options: monthly or annual reserved capacity. For Dedicated we commonly see customers choose a 6–12 month commit to get significant discounts; however we can do month-to-month reserved pools for smaller commits. Lead time: usually 2–4 weeks to provision a dedicated pool depending on size and region. Aditya can confirm technical lead time for your expected throughput.

> 3) Marketplace: AWS Marketplace would make approvals much easier for us — do you support Marketplace billing for Dedicated capacity or is it only for hosted API?

We support AWS Marketplace for both hosted API and Dedicated (in many configurations) — it depends on the procurement flow you choose. Marketplace can be used for subscription/commit purchases which then map to reserved capacity. We’ll surface the Marketplace SKU if you want to pursue that route.

I attached a sample SOW and the PO template you can share with legal/finance (RWI-SOW-draft.docx; Acme-PO-Template.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the procurement owner/contact and any internal deadlines for onboarding.
- I’ll draft a short mutual action plan with milestone that triggers PO for production (and include Marketplace SKU option).
- Aditya, can you confirm the 2–4 week provisioning estimate for Dedicated and whether any extra security integrations (VPC peering, KMS) would add time?

Thanks — I’ll prepare the MAP + SOW draft once Tom confirms procurement contact.

Best,
Marissa
[Attachment: RWI-SOW-draft.docx]
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Evans <tom.evans@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & procurement paths (hosted / dedicated / private)

Hi Tom — quick technical note from our side and recommendation for low-friction procurement: 

- Provisioning: For the POC on hosted there’s no provisioning lead time beyond getting API keys (minutes/hours). For Dedicated pools, 2–3 weeks is typical for standard configurations; add 1–2 weeks if you require private networking (VPC peering) or custom KMS/HSM integration.
- Migration path: We’ve done the hosted->dedicated transition for several retailers. The flow is: validate on hosted, reserve committed capacity (via Marketplace or PO), then we perform a configuration cutover where traffic is routed to dedicated pools; KV cache warming and rolling cutover usually completed within a day.
- Marketplace: if Acme wants Marketplace, we can surface SKU and Professional Services can help with procurement packaging to meet your internal procurement PO workflow.

Rachel (cc) will own onboarding and can provide a proposed MAP with dates once we have the procurement owner and desired go-live window.

If useful, I can jump on a short call with procurement next week to walk through the Marketplace option and provisioning timelines.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
